Tesaro looks toward China to undercut in first-line maintenance for ovarian cancer
Company: Tesaro, Inc. (TSRO)
Therapy: Niraparib
Disease: Ovarian cancer
News: TSRO’s partner in China Zai Lab announced that it has commenced dosing of its PARP inhibitor niraparib (branded Zejula) as first-line “maintenance” therapy in patients who respond to platinum-based chemotherapy (Note: Maintenance refers to giving one or more relatively safe drugs for a long period of time, or indefinitely, in order to preserve disease control for as long as possible). This study will be conducted with the intention of pursuing approval for this indication in China.
Looking forward: There are no PARP inhibitors approved in China yet, but it’s not for lack of trying. AstraZeneca (AZN) and Merck (MRK) are trying their darnedest, and upstart competitor BeiGene (BGNE) has its own PARP inhibitor trial ongoing. This gives TSRO an opportunity to attack in a space where we already know PARP inhibitors can be successful, given that we just saw benefit in the first-line maintenance setting for olaparib. Shares of Apple Inc. (Nasdaq: AAPL) may face additional pressure today after another surprise update from one of its biggest suppliers. Austria-based supplier AMS, a maker of optical sensors for the iPhone X, warned that sales for the second quarter will fall by roughly 50% from the first quarter. This comes not long after Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. Ltd.(ADR) (NYSE: TSM) offered a lower-than-expected Q2 revenue forecast. Now, Wall Street analysts could soon follow with cuts to iPhone sales forecasts, especially after rival Samsung warned of a slowdown in display panel sales. This morning, the European Central Bank announced it will maintain its record-low interest rates and accommodating monetary policy. At a time when the U.S. central bank is raising rates, the ECB failed to provide a timeline on when it will end its massive stimulus package, which features monthly bond purchases of $37 billion.
